event.text: IBM presented the first program-controlled calculator to Harvard University, after which it became known as the Mark I (pictured).
event.page_extract: International Business Machines Corporation, doing business as IBM, is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Armonk, New York, and present in over 175 countries. It is a publicly traded company and one of the 30 companies in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. IBM is the largest industrial research organization in the world, with 19 research facilities across a dozen countries; for 29 consecutive years, from 1993 to 2021, it held the record for most annual U.S. patents generated by a business.

title: The Gift of Logic, MCMXLIV
artist_statement: I remember the silence of that room, the way the air smelled of oil and copper. There was no fanfare—just a quiet handing over of something enormous. The machine was a kind of altar, and I wanted to paint the stillness that surrounded it, the weight of all that unspoken understanding.
image_prompt: A high-ceilinged, wood-paneled room at dusk, lit only by a single brass lamp with a green glass shade. Its cone of warm light falls on a vast, rectilinear machine of polished metal and glass, its face a grid of dials and switches. Two men in dark suits stand before it, one with a hand resting on the machine’s edge, the other with his arms folded, both gazing at it without speaking. Dust motes hang in the lamplight. The palette is deep browns, tarnished brass, and shadowy indigo. The brushwork is visible and restrained, like a Hopper interior—quiet, expectant, reverent.
